My land is 70 mu. The wheat and maize rotate on the same 40 mu — wheat goes in after autumn, maize goes in after the wheat harvest in June. The other 30 mu I split between the cash crops: cauliflower, chili, cotton, watermelon. These bring better money than grain, but they need more work and water from the well.

I have been doing this six years now. I know what sells at the Quzhou market, and I know what my well can handle in a dry summer. I do not experiment much. I plant what I know, buy the seeds the village agronomist recommends, and follow what the neighbors do. My family is three people — me, my wife, and one child — so I need stable income from wheat and maize to cover the basics, and the vegetables to get ahead.

For wheat I use an improved variety like Jimai or Kenong, whatever the seed shop is pushing this year. Nitrogen goes in heavy — that is how everyone does it here. I irrigate wheat four times: at sowing, in early spring when it greens up, at jointing, and at heading. For maize I plant a hybrid, 先玉335 or 郑单958, right after the wheat comes off in June. Summer has more rain so I irrigate less. Cotton I plant Bt hybrid — saves me spraying for bollworm. Watermelon goes in early spring, needs good potassium and regular water. Cauliflower I plant in autumn on 8 mu. Chili I squeeze into the summer alongside the maize and cotton on the remaining land.

I keep pesticide applications down on Bt cotton but spray more on the vegetables, which get aphids and rot every year.
